text:
Alex Laferriere is doing the work and getting almost nothing for it. The former third-round pick out of Harvard is playing 19:23 a night, he's on the ice for 72% of the Kings' power-play chances (up from 30%), and his own chances have jumped to 1.42 expected goals per 60, a measure of how good his looks are, from 0.96 last season. He has three goals to show for 8.25 expected. He's shooting 5.5% against a league norm around 13%.

The bad luck spreads past his own stick. Los Angeles has scored 5.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, even though the Kings get 58% of the expected goals at five-on-five in his minutes. Seven shots against Ottawa, seven against Pittsburgh, five against Calgary: the volume is there, and it has come in a stretch when the Kings have lost a lot. Eighteen games is a small sample, and ice time settles faster than scoring, but if you only look at his 13 points you're missing how much more he's doing this year.
